response.why: Attacking is low-risk here: their only possible blocker is one summoning-sick-but-blocking-legal Eddymurk Crab, so at worst we trade a Crab evenly or lose Hearth Elemental for no return, while unblocked lines put them at 3-4 life with our board intact. Holding Hearth Elemental back as a blocker while swinging both Crabs (leaves 8-9) is safest since even the trade-off leaf only costs us an even Crab trade and keeps a full-health blocker up; full attack risks a bad Hearth-Elemental-for-nothing trade but pushes opponent closer to lethal in the same turn. Not attacking wastes a nearly free damage swing against an empty-handed opponent.
response.plan: Attack with all three creatures (or at minimum both Crabs, holding Hearth Elemental back) since their only blocker can't stop us from getting to lethal range this turn or next; holding Spell Snare in reserve for any relevant 2-mana spell they topdeck.

response.why: Opponent is at 4 life with an empty hand and only a single non-lethal creature (Hearth Elemental, 5 toughness survives any of our 3-damage effects), so nothing they can do here threatens us. Casting Glacial Dragonhunt for a cantrip (discard: none) is best since its 2 mana cost leaves exactly 1 land up for Spell Snare against their Harmonize Glacial Dragonhunt recast (mana value 2) if it matters, giving both card advantage and interaction; casting Winternight Stories nets bigger card selection but taps us out, forfeiting Spell Snare, which is an acceptable but slightly worse trade since their spell is harmless anyway. Discarding Winternight Stories to Glacial Dragonhunt's trigger is the worst use of resources since 3 damage can't kill anything on their side and burns a full card for no real gain.
response.plan: Cast Glacial Dragonhunt discarding nothing (or a spare land if a nonland discard is forced) to draw a card while keeping 1 mana open for Spell Snare against their Harmonize recast; not spending Spell Snare on the harmless 3-damage trigger itself since our creatures can't be killed by it.

response.why: The attack this turn is already guaranteed lethal regardless of this main-phase choice (opponent has zero mana and only one legal blocker, and either of our two attackers alone deals enough unblocked damage to kill them at 4 life), so nearly every line here is fine. Casting Burst Lightning to the face for 2 (or kicked for 4, if somehow affordable) is best since it either finishes the game immediately in main phase or banks extra insurance before combat even happens; several lines that also draw into extra burn or benefit from the opponent's own life-payment land drops reach opp_life 0 outright. Discarding a freshly-drawn Glacial Dragonhunt to its own trigger for a non-lethal 3-damage ping is the weakest choice since it wastes a full card for no real gain given the attack already wins.
response.plan: Cast Burst Lightning at the opponent's face (kicked if mana allows, otherwise unkicked) for guaranteed extra damage, then proceed to combat and attack with Eddymurk Crab and the original Hearth Elemental for lethal regardless.
